label: Propofol PD — effect-site → BIS sigmoid Emax

extraction.tier_rationale: Population-mean BIS Ce50 with wide reported spread; representative, not validated for any individual.

known_failure_modes.condition: BIS is an EEG-derived index with device-specific behaviour and known artefacts
known_failure_modes.behavior: Population-mean sigmoid cannot represent individual hysteresis or processed-EEG artefact; for research comparison only.

extraction.tier_rationale: Single-purpose population-mean sigmoid Emax for BIS; large between-subject variability and device dependence place it at Tier C. Useful for divergence/illustration, not prediction.

source_review.reviewed_by: automated source cross-check (Claude Opus 4.8 via Hypnos research agents)
source_review.method: fetched open-source reproductions, primary-paper PubMed abstracts, and/or the tci R package source, then numerically compared each curated value against the fetched values
sources: open PD-model reproductions (Bouillon/Vuyk BIS sigmoid: Ce50~4.47, gamma 1.43)
source_review.notes: CITATION/ATTRIBUTION DISCREPANCY (values NOT changed): the cited Schnider 1999 paper ('The influence of age on propofol pharmacodynamics', Anesthesiology 90:1502) does NOT model BIS — it uses semilinear canonical correlation and reports age-dependent loss-of-consciousness C50 (2.35/1.8/1.25 ug/mL at 25/50/75 y), NOT E0=93/Emax=93/Ce50=4.7/gamma=1.43. The curated Ce50~4.7 and gamma 1.43 match a Bouillon/Vuyk-style propofol->BIS sigmoid, not Schnider 1999. HUMAN ACTION: re-cite this propofol->BIS sigmoid to its true source (e.g. Bouillon 2004 / Vuyk) or confirm the values+citation pairing.

notes: E = E0 - Emax * Ce^gamma / (Ce50^gamma + Ce^gamma). Pairs with any propofol PK model's effect-site output to produce a BIS trajectory; the composed simulation inherits this Tier-C floor.
